about: The non-circular run. The two readers of paper-two-readers-2026-09-13 were both written here, and the careful one was written after seeing what the plain one missed, so its 100 % measured its author. This puts a reader through the bench that was written from the JATS standard and not from the bench: lxml and the canonical XPaths of article-meta.

reader.built_from: lxml 6.1.1 and the canonical JATS paths
reader.note: Not one of these paths was chosen by looking at what the bench injects. They are the paths anyone writes who opens the JATS documentation and follows article-meta.

pre_registered_before_the_run.predicted_total: about 71.4 %, the same as the plain reader
predicted_blind_spots: form-107, because a node list taken at [0] returns the first DOI
form-120, because it reads contrib and the second spelling is in alt-title

corpus: 300 Europe PMC JATS articles held locally
reading: 71.3 % against 71.4 % predicted, and the two blind spots are the two named before the run.

The standard way of reading JATS is blind to two faults a real corpus carries at 9 % and 8.5 %, measured 2026-08-08 on 272 articles. The blindness is structural and not accidental: a second declaration exists in the document and the path stops at the first, and a second spelling of an author exists in the document and the path does not go there.
This is not a criticism of lxml nor of anyone. Where a reader looks is a design decision that nobody writes down, and it fixes what the graph downstream can ever contain.
the one departure from the prediction: form-198 came back 299 of 300 and not 300. One document held. Not investigated; it is the same shape as the 13 documents whose epub and ppub years differ, where damaging the declarations of one value leaves the other standing.
what it still does not say: It does not measure p. No house filter runs in this pass either.
